item.title: Micron beats on revenue and EPS, guides first-quarter revenue well above estimates
item.description:
The guidance matters more than the quarter itself, because it suggests memory demand and pricing are running ahead of what the market had priced in. A first-quarter revenue outlook well above consensus is likely to keep attention on chipmakers tied to data-centre spending. Asian memory producers, which often trade in sympathy with Micron's read on pricing, are also in focus. The softer guided gross margin is the one detail that could temper enthusiasm, so call commentary on supply, pricing and capital spending will shape how the shares and the wider sector react.

-

Micron beat on every headline measure and guided revenue sharply higher, with automotive and embedded the standout and a slightly lighter margin outlook the only blemish.

Summary:

  • Fourth-quarter adjusted revenue was around $54.2 billion, against expectations of roughly $51 billion.
  • Adjusted EPS came in near $33.40, ahead of estimates of a little under $32.
  • Adjusted gross margin was 87%, versus an expected 86.2%.
  • Cloud Memory revenue was about $16.3 billion (expected $15.1 billion), Mobile & Client about $13.1 billion (expected $13.0 billion), and Automotive & Embedded about $6.8 billion (expected $4.7 billion).
  • First-quarter revenue is guided to $60 billion to $63 billion, against expectations of around $57 billion.
  • First-quarter adjusted EPS is guided to roughly $37 to $39, against expectations of about $35.40 to $36, while the guided gross margin of around 86% is below the 87% expected.

Micron Technology reported fourth-quarter results that beat analyst expectations on revenue, earnings and margin, and followed them with a first-quarter outlook well ahead of consensus. Adjusted revenue was around $54.2 billion, compared with estimates of roughly $51 billion, while adjusted earnings per share of near $33.40 were above forecasts of a little under $32.

Profitability also held up strongly. Adjusted gross margin came in at 87%, slightly better than the 86.2% the market was looking for, suggesting the revenue upside was not bought at the expense of pricing or cost discipline.

The segment breakdown showed strength across the business, with the largest surprise outside the core memory franchise. Automotive and Embedded revenue reached about $6.8 billion, far above expectations of roughly $4.7 billion, a gap of more than 40%. Cloud Memory revenue of about $16.3 billion beat the $15.1 billion estimate by a little over $1 billion, while Mobile & Client sales of around $13.1 billion were only modestly ahead of the $13.0 billion forecast. That pattern points to demand that is broadening rather than resting on a single end market, although a single quarter is not enough to call it a trend.

The forward guidance carried the most weight. Micron expects first-quarter revenue of $60 billion to $63 billion, with a midpoint of $61.5 billion, compared with consensus of around $57 billion. It guided adjusted EPS of about $37 to $39, also above expectations in the $35 to $36 area. Guidance at that level implies sequential revenue growth of more than 10% at the midpoint, a fast pace for a company of this size.

One detail runs against the otherwise strong tone. The guided first-quarter gross margin of around 86% sits below the 87% analysts had expected, and is slightly under the 87% just reported. The shortfall is small, but it means investors will look to management commentary for an explanation, whether that is product mix, costs or pricing assumptions.

Attention now turns to the earnings call, where comments on supply, pricing and capital spending plans are likely to shape how the market reads both the beat and the outlook. 

This article was written by Eamonn Sheridan at investinglive.com.

Analysis: Trump is turning the Fed renovation dispute into another pressure point against Powell. The key development is his statement that he has asked the attorney general to review the report and determine what action to take. That goes beyond criticism of construction costs, although the post does not establish that a lawsuit or other legal action has been initiated.

For traders, the issue is whether that review develops into a broader challenge to the Fed’s ability to make policy decisions without political pressure. The construction allegations themselves do not tell us where interest rates are heading. Also, Trump’s suggestion that the final bill could reach $3.5 billion or $4 billion is his own projection, distinct from the $2.5 billion figure he attributes to the report.

The next question is what the review produces and how the Fed responds.  In his favorite words, it sounds like a witch hunt.

item.title: The USDCAD reverses back higher after the sellers failed to take short term control
item.description:
The USDCAD has been trending higher since bottoming on September 8. Over that stretch, the price has climbed from 1.3759 to a fresh monthly high of 1.4224, reached within the last hour of trading. That represents a gain of 465 pips, or approximately 3.38%.

Today, however, sellers had an opportunity to interrupt that trend.

They had their shot. They missed.

The downside break failed to find follow-through

During the late Asian-Pacific and early European sessions, the price broke below a rising trendline near 1.4192. The selling then pushed the pair below its 100-hour moving average, currently at 1.4168, and down to a session low of 1.4155.

Those breaks gave sellers an opening. Breaking the trendline was the first step. Moving below the 100-hour moving average added to the downside argument. What sellers needed next was continued momentum toward the swing area between 1.41297 and 1.41488.

That did not happen.

The price stalled before reaching that area and reversed higher. Sellers turned back into buyers, and the rebound carried the pair back above the 100-hour moving average and the broken trendline.

Over the last six hours or so, that upside momentum has continued, taking the price to a new monthly high at 1.4224.

The failed downside break puts the buyers back in control.

Buyers approach the next major resistance area

The rally is now moving closer to the June and early July highs between 1.42385 and 1.42474.

That area represents the next key test. After a 465-pip advance from the September low, traders may look to take some profit against those prior highs. Sellers may also lean against the area, using a sustained break above it to define their risk.

For buyers, the task is straightforward: break above the highs and stay above them.

A sustained move above 1.42474 would take the USDCAD to its highest level since April 2025 and open the door toward 1.42928. That level represents the 61.8% retracement of the decline from the February 2025 high to the January 2026 low.

What would take control away from the buyers?

On a pullback, the trendline near 1.4192 is an initial reference, although that level rises over time. Below it, the 100-hour moving average at 1.4168 remains a key short-term barometer.

A move back below that moving average—and sustained trading below it—would weaken the renewed bullish bias. Sellers would then need to push below today’s 1.4155 low to demonstrate that they can build on the break.

That would bring the 1.41297–1.41488 swing area back into focus.

Today’s price action showed that breaking a technical level is only part of the job. Sellers also need to keep the price below it and extend toward the next target. Without that follow-through, control can quickly shift back to the other side.

Key technical levels

  • 1.42928: 61.8% retracement and next upside target above the June/July highs.

  • 1.42385–1.42474: June and early July highs; next major resistance area.

  • 1.4224: Fresh monthly high.

  • Near 1.4192: Rising trendline reference from earlier today.

  • 1.4168: 100-hour moving average.

  • 1.4155: Today’s low.

  • 1.41297–1.41488: Key swing support area.

A lesson for beginner traders

A break below support can look convincing, especially when the price crosses both a trendline and a moving average. But the next question matters just as much: Can the sellers keep the price below those levels?

Today, the answer was no. The downside move stalled before the next support area, and the price reclaimed the broken levels. That recovery was a warning that the sellers’ advantage was fading.

Technical levels help traders define risk, but follow-through helps confirm control. Today, the failed break and subsequent new high shifted that control back to the buyers.

In the video above, I take a closer look at the failed downside break, the buyers’ recovery, and the levels that will help determine whether the USDCAD can extend its trend higher.

This article was written by Greg Michalowski at investinglive.com.

item.title: USDCHF is up for the 6th straight day and trading near the highest level since May 2025
item.description:
The USDCHF is trading up 0.12% on the day, putting the pair on track for its sixth consecutive daily gain. The rally has carried the price from a recent low of 0.81822 to yesterday’s high of 0.83580, a gain of approximately 2.15%, or 176 pips.

That is a solid move in a short period of time. However, the buyers have now reached a level where they need to prove they can keep the momentum going.

Policy divergence supports the dollar

Fundamentally, the Swiss National Bank left rates unchanged at its latest meeting. In contrast, the Federal Reserve raised rates by 25 basis points and signaled that another hike could come before year-end.

With the market pricing in around a 40% chance of an October hike and a near-100% chance of a hike by year-end, the policy divergence provides a supportive backdrop for the dollar against the Swiss franc.

But a supportive fundamental story does not eliminate the potential for a technical correction—particularly after six days of gains and with the price testing a key resistance level.

Buyers have tested resistance twice. Can they stay above?

Yesterday’s rally reached 0.83580, briefly taking the price above the May 29, 2025 high at 0.83485. However, buyers could not sustain the break, and the pair closed back below that level.

Today, buyers had another shot. The price pushed above 0.83485 to an intraday high of 0.83540, but again backed off. The pair is now trading right around that old high as traders weigh the next move.

Does the rally extend, or is the pair ready for a corrective move lower?

For buyers, the requirement is straightforward: get above 0.83485 and stay above. A move through today’s high at 0.83540 and yesterday’s high at 0.83580 would strengthen the bullish case and open the door toward 0.8400.

That level is both natural round-number resistance and the 50% midpoint of the decline from the February 2025 high to the January 2026 low, making it the next key upside target.

What would give sellers more control?

If resistance continues to hold, the first important downside test comes against the rising 100-hour moving average at 0.83134.

A pullback toward that moving average would give buyers an opportunity to defend the trend. Hold above it, and they retain the technical advantage.

However, a break below 0.83134—and sustained trading below—would give sellers more control and increase the potential for a deeper correction toward the rising 200-hour moving average at 0.82699.

Key technical levels to eye

  • 0.84000: 50% retracement and round-number resistance.

  • 0.83580: Yesterday’s high.

  • 0.83540: Today’s high.

  • 0.83485: May 29, 2025 high and immediate pivot.

  • 0.83134: Rising 100-hour moving average; first key downside support.

  • 0.82699: Rising 200-hour moving average; next corrective target.

Beginner trader takeaway

A price can briefly move above resistance without confirming a breakout. Yesterday and today, the USDCHF traded above 0.83485, but each move attracted selling.

That is why I emphasize “break and stay above.” The break shows buyers are trying. Staying above shows they are succeeding.

The buyers still have the trend in their favor. Now they need to turn 0.83485 from resistance into support to keep the run going.

This article was written by Greg Michalowski at investinglive.com.

item.title: Goldman Sachs moves its call for the next Fed rate hike to December from October
item.description:
Goldman Sachs has changed its forecast for the next Fed rate hike from October to December.

Yesterday, John Williams, the New York Fed president and a permanent FOMC voter, said one more rate hike this year may be enough, provided the economy develops as expected. However, he sees “no need for urgency” after September’s hike, giving the Fed time to review more data before acting again.

His outlook includes:

  • Growth: GDP rising 2.25% this year, with economic momentum strong and potentially strengthening.
  • Employment: Unemployment at 4% during 2027.
  • Inflation: 3.5% this year, returning to the 2% target in 2028.
  • Risks: Growing AI investment could add inflation pressure. The Fed must prevent supply shocks from making higher inflation persistent.

The message on October: Williams did not rule out a hike, but his comments supported the possibility of waiting. At the time, the October hike odds fell to 54% from 64%, while the US 2-year yield declined 2.5 basis points to 4.90%. Today, the odds for a hike are down to 40% with the 2 year yield at 4.887%

Although Williams’ comments were viewed as more dovish, his outlook remains conditional. Incoming data will determine both whether another rate hike is needed and when it might come.

Another consideration is the calendar. The October meeting falls at the end of the month, less than a week before the November midterm elections. In my view, a hike that close to Election Day could invite criticism from President Trump and other Republicans that the Fed was trying to influence the results. That does not mean the Fed would avoid a necessary move, but it adds political sensitivity to the timing.

Meanwhile, the market is already doing some of the tightening for the Fed. The 10-year yield has risen from around 4.61% on August 25 to 5.293% currently (see chart below), an increase of roughly 67 basis points—nearly 68 basis points. The 2-year yield has climbed from 4.26% on August 13 to 4.89%, a rise of 63 basis points.

Those higher yields tighten financial conditions by raising borrowing costs for households and businesses. That could give the Fed an argument for pausing in October while it assesses the incoming data and the impact of the tightening already delivered by the bond market.

This article was written by Greg Michalowski at investinglive.com.

item.title: ECB’s Schnabel: High costs passed through to consumers more quickly when economy resilient
item.description:
Comments from the ECB’s Schnabel cross the wires:

  • High costs passed through to consumers more quickly when economy resilient.
  • Robust credit dynamics suggest that financial conditions are not yet restrictive.
  • Possible economy responds more to the recent global yield rise than assumed; would dampen price pressures.
  • Can return inflation to target more gradually when expectations anchored.

Analysis: The message is mixed. A resilient economy allows businesses to pass higher costs through to consumers more quickly, keeping inflation pressures in play. Meanwhile, robust credit growth suggests financial conditions are not yet restrictive. Those comments lean hawkish, as they question how much monetary policy is restraining demand.

However, Schnabel also leaves room for patience. Higher global yields could slow the economy more than expected, helping ease price pressures. If inflation expectations remain anchored—meaning households and businesses still expect inflation to return to target—the ECB can take a more gradual approach. The key question is whether higher borrowing costs start to restrain demand, or whether economic resilience keeps the cost increases flowing through to consumers.

This article was written by Greg Michalowski at investinglive.com.
